How many GB of space would a Linux installation partition require?

Your root (/) partition (roughly equivalent of C:\ in Windows) can take up as little as 1 GB. You can even boot from a live CD/USB without the need of installing the system on your drive. Generally, it's a matter of what do you want to have installed. Look up Linux partitioning, learn about /, /boot, /home, /var and swap partitions.

I have a windows machine I put together myself with parts for gaming, and I'm also an advocate for our rights as an American, tired of the media and government lying to us manipulating us spying on us etc. Tired of the tech companies doing it too. Anyways, would anyone have a recommendation of the best place to start learning Linux for the first time ever, for someone with decently in depth knowledge of windows compared to the average user? I'd need to also know how to run windows as a VM on linux to continue to game, if necessary.
After privacy concerns on Windows 7 after all the updates that cause it to resemble 10, I'd really like to learn more into how I can transform my Windows machine into Linux.

People have their own preferences on what Linux distro to use, you can't go terribly wrong (as long as you don't dive in to a more difficult distro like slackware), but i would recommend to try Ubuntu first. If you can't find someone with the same issue (almost never happens, search your error message etc and you will find forum posts about the issue), someone is always eager to respond if you post your issue to their forum, or here for that matter.

To run windows on a VM, just look here!

I would suggest you start by switching all your applications (besides games) to equivalent with cross-platform support. So switch to LibreOffice, Firefox, Thunderbird, etc. You can keep that up as long as you want even if you stick to Windows as operating system.

The next step would be to try out Linux for yourself, and in this I would recommend you start with one of the distributions that provide "Live CD" or "Live USB" images that you can set up to boot from instead of the main disk. It can give you a feeling of what Linux is like without having to go through partitioning/installation. Some also offer permanence, so that across multiple boots you'll keep any changes you make.

to get you up and running quickly I would recommend Ubuntu. Ubuntu is a ready to go distro with all the bells and whistles that a new user would come to expect. They have a great support form http://askubuntu.com/ which is quick to help. Now for actually learning linux I would say to read the documentation and guides over on the Arch wiki. Its not a distro I personally use but they have some of the best documentation on packages and configurations. Most of the information there can be used universally among distros https://wiki.archlinux.org/ . I use VMware Workstation for my Windows VM not that it is the only option you have but I have just found it to work the best for getting the most out of my VM. You can download a free 30 day trial: http://www.vmware.com/products/workstation They also have the free VMware player. VirtualBox is another great one with nice features https://www.virtualbox.org/.

Good luck and don't be afraid to ask questions!

Dual boot means that you have two separate operating systems on the same machine. You can have more. The laptop i am typing on is running Mint 17.2 Cinnamon but also has Windows 10 (games only) windows 8 (factory install) and Kali Linux. Linux does not have to suppress anything because when you are booted into Linux, Windows is not running and cannot take any actions because the two are fundamentally different. I would recommend using the built-in installer in Linux Mint or Ubuntu to partition your drive and set up the dual boot. It will install the vastly superior Linux bootloader Grub2 in the process which will ask you at power on which system you would like to boot up. Obviously back your important files up before making major changes like this but it is fairly unlikely you will run into trouble. And of course if you do, just post here and someone will surely help you out. Good luck.
